title: Equivalence of PBC and IA
statement:
For a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f$, the following
conditions are equivalent.

1. $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ holds in the sense of
   [def-weil-pbc-property].
2. $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ holds for every prime $r$ in the sense of
   [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property].

proof.text: The implication $\mathrm{PBC}(f)\Rightarrow\mathrm{IA}(f)$ is the reusable direction [lem-weil-pbc-property-implies-acyclicity]. It applies PBC to an injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf in degree zero, uses module-to-abelian direct-image acyclicity and exact inverse image, and transfers the resulting vanishing across the specified exchange isomorphism for every base change.

Conversely assume $\mathrm{IA}(f)$. For an $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $E$,
take an injective resolution $E\to I^\bullet$. Acyclicity and
[lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] make $f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet$ compute
$Rf'_*g'^{-1}E$, while $g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet$ computes $g^{-1}Rf_*E$; the
underived proper exchange of [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange] is an
isomorphism in every degree, and by naturality these maps form an isomorphism
of complexes, which is the derived exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. For a sheaf $F$ killed by $n$,
induction on the number of prime factors of $n$ using the exact sequence of
[lem-weil-pbc-prime-factor-devissage] and the five-lemma transfer of
[lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer] gives the assertion for $F[n]$. Finally
every torsion sheaf is the filtered union of the $F[n]$ by
[lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union], and
[lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] passes the isomorphism to the
colimit, since proper maps are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. This proves
$\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ by [def-weil-pbc-property].

blueprint_sketch.statement: For proper $f$, $\mathsf{PBC}(f)$ holds if and only if $\mathsf{IA}(f)$ holds.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Assume $\mathsf{PBC}(f)$. For an injective $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf
$I$ and a base change $g$, apply
the isomorphism to the complex concentrated in degree zero. The source has
no higher cohomology because $I$ is injective, so the target has none; this is
the required acyclicity. Conversely assume $\mathsf{IA}(f)$. Resolve any
torsion $F$ by injectives $I^\bullet$. The inverse image complex
$g'^{-1}I^\bullet$ computes $Rf'_*g'^{-1}F$ because each term is acyclic.
For an $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf $E$, choose an injective resolution
$E\to I^\bullet$ in the $\mathbf F_\ell$-module category. IA makes every
$g'^{-1}I^r$ $f'_*$-acyclic, so Lemma
[lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] identifies the target of the derived
exchange map with the cohomology of $f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet$. In each degree,
the underived proper exchange lemma gives an isomorphism

$$
g^{-1}f_*I^r\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*g'^{-1}I^r,
$$

and the replacement-independence lemma makes these maps a morphism of the
chosen resolutions. Thus $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,E}$ is an isomorphism.
For $F[n]$, the prime-factor induction lemma and the five-lemma transfer
propagate this isomorphism through the exact sequences
$0\to F[\ell]\to F[n]\xrightarrow{\ell}\ell F[n]\to0$; the induction
parameter is $\nu(n)=\sum_\ell v_\ell(n)$, with the prime-torsion case just
proved. Finally $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ by the filtered torsion-union lemma.
The filtered-colimit direct-image lemma applies after every quasi-compact
etale base change, so it identifies both cohomology sheaves and carries the
isomorphisms for the $F[n]$ to the specified map $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$.
This proves PBC for every torsion sheaf and closes the converse implication.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a proper morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] $f$, the following
conditions are equivalent.

1. $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ holds for torsion coefficients: for every cartesian square
   [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] over $f$ and every
   $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves whose cohomology sheaves are torsion
   [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], the derived exchange morphism
   $\Ex_{\square,K}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is an isomorphism (the
   property of [def-weil-pbc-property] restricted to objects with torsion
   cohomology).
2. $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ holds for every prime $r$ in the sense of
   [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property].

proof.text:
Suppose $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ holds. Restriction of scalars along
$\mathbf Z\to\mathbf F_r$ is exact and conservative, commutes with inverse and
direct images and with derived direct images (an injective sheaf of
$\mathbf F_r$-modules has no higher cohomology as an abelian sheaf), and a
complex of sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules has torsion cohomology; so it
carries the exchange morphism over $\mathbf F_r$ to the one over $\mathbf Z$, and
$\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ gives the base change property with $\mathbf F_r$-coefficients.
If $I$ is injective among $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaves, then $Rf_*I=f_*I$; after
arbitrary base change, this base change property identifies $Rf'_*g'^{-1}I$ with
the degree-zero complex $g^{-1}f_*I$, so $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for $q>0$, which is
$\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ by [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property].

Conversely assume $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ for every prime $r$. Fix $r$ and
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$, and represent $K$ by a bounded below complex
$I^\bullet$ of injective sheaves of $\mathbf F_r$-modules. Then
$g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet$ computes $g^{-1}Rf_*K$. The terms of $g'^{-1}I^\bullet$
are $f'_*$-acyclic by $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$, so by
[lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] $f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet$ computes
$Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$. Under these identifications the derived exchange morphism of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the underived proper exchange
$g^{-1}f_*I^\bullet\to f'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet$ of
[lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange], an isomorphism in every degree.
So the base change property holds with $\mathbf F_r$-coefficients.

Now let $E$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ killed by a prime $r$. Then $E$ is
the restriction of scalars of an $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf, and restriction of
scalars carries the exchange morphism over $\mathbf F_r$ to the one over
$\mathbf Z$ (see the first paragraph); hence $\Ex^q_{\square,E}$ is an
isomorphism for every $q$. Since proper maps are quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, the prime-torsion devissage
[lemma-weil-pbc-prime-torsion-devissage] shows that $\Ex^q_{\square,F}$ is an
isomorphism for every $q$ and every torsion sheaf $F$. For
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ with torsion cohomology, induction on the
length of the canonical truncations of $K$ (both $g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}$
are triangulated and send $D^{\geq N}$ into $D^{\geq N}$) shows that
$\Ex_{\square,K}$ is an isomorphism in every degree. This proves (1).
